name: LIS3MDL 3-axis magnetometer
description: STMicroelectronics 3-axis magnetometer (compass sensor) with selectable ±4/±8/±12/±16 gauss full scale, 16-bit output, I2C or SPI. Chip runs on 1.9–3.6 V; the breakout has a 3.3 V regulator and level shifting for 3–5 V. Sold as: Adafruit Triple-axis Magnetometer - LIS3MDL (#4479, STEMMA QT; 6-pin header VIN, 3Vo, GND, SCL, SDA, INT and 4-pin header GND, DRDY, DO, CS), I2C address 0x1C (0x1E with DO/AD1 high).
eli5: Feels magnetic fields in three directions, so your project can tell which way is north or notice a nearby magnet.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply, 3–5 V (on-board AP2112K 3.3 V regulator; use your board's logic voltage)

pins.name: 3Vo
pins.description: 3.3 V output of the on-board regulator (up to 100 mA); not a supply input, leave unconnected

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (SPI clock in SPI mode); level-shifted, 10 kΩ pull-up on the board

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (SPI data in in SPI mode); level-shifted, 10 kΩ pull-up on the board

pins.name: INT
pins.description: Interrupt output (threshold events), not needed for basic use

pins.name: GND2
pins.description: Second ground pin, on the other header (printed GND)

pins.name: DRDY
pins.description: Data-ready output, not needed for basic use

pins.name: DO
pins.description: I2C address select SDO/SA1 (AD1): 10 kΩ to GND on the board = 0x1C, tie to 3Vo = 0x1E; SPI data out in SPI mode

pins.name: CS
pins.description: SPI chip select; pulled up on the board so I2C is used, leave unconnected for I2C

buildNotes: The board has two headers on opposite edges (VIN, 3Vo, GND, SCL, SDA, INT and GND, DRDY, DO, CS); for I2C you only need VIN, GND, SCL and SDA.
Reset default is power-down (CTRL_REG3 = 0x03): write CTRL_REG3 = 0x00 for continuous conversion or every reading stays 0.
Read the six output bytes in one burst from register 0x28 | 0x80 (the top bit asks for auto-increment); values are 16-bit two's complement, low byte first.
At the default ±4 gauss full scale the sensitivity is 6842 LSB/gauss (±8: 3421, ±12: 2281, ±16: 1711). Earth's field is about 0.25–0.65 gauss.

Address 0x1C as shipped; tie DO (AD1) to 3Vo or bridge the jumper on the back for 0x1E. Adafruit notes a few boards read the address erratically with only the 10 kΩ pull-down: tie DO firmly to GND if so.
Keep it away from motors, speakers, steel screws and current-carrying wires, which swamp the Earth's field.

driver.code:
# LIS3MDL 3-axis magnetometer (STMicroelectronics), MicroPython driver.
# Written from the ST datasheet DocID024204 Rev 4: WHO_AM_I 0x0F = 0x3D, CTRL_REG1..5 at 0x20..0x24,
# STATUS_REG 0x27, OUT_X_L..OUT_Z_H at 0x28..0x2D (two's complement, LSB at the lower address).
# In I2C the MSb of the register address asks for auto-increment, so a 6-byte burst starts at 0x28 | 0x80.
import time

_WHO_AM_I = 0x0F
_CTRL_REG1 = 0x20
_CTRL_REG2 = 0x21
_CTRL_REG3 = 0x22
_CTRL_REG4 = 0x23
_CTRL_REG5 = 0x24
_STATUS_REG = 0x27
_OUT_X_L = 0x28

# Full scale (gauss) -> (FS[1:0] bits for CTRL_REG2, sensitivity in LSB/gauss), datasheet Tables 3 and 25.
_RANGES = {4: (0x00, 6842), 8: (0x20, 3421), 12: (0x40, 2281), 16: (0x60, 1711)}


class LIS3MDL:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x1C, range_gauss=4):
        """addr 0x1C with SDO/SA1 (the board's DO pin) low, 0x1E with it high."""
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        who = self._r(_WHO_AM_I, 1)[0]
        if who != 0x3D:
            raise OSError('LIS3MDL not found (WHO_AM_I=0x%02X): check wiring and address' % who)
        if range_gauss not in _RANGES:
            raise ValueError('range_gauss must be 4, 8, 12 or 16')
        fs_bits, self._sens = _RANGES[range_gauss]
        # CTRL_REG1: TEMP_EN=0, OM=11 (X/Y ultra-high-performance), DO=100 (10 Hz), FAST_ODR=0, ST=0
        self._w(_CTRL_REG1, 0x70)
        # CTRL_REG2: full scale (other bits must be 0)
        self._w(_CTRL_REG2, fs_bits)
        # CTRL_REG4: OMZ=11 (Z ultra-high-performance), BLE=0 (LSB at lower address)
        self._w(_CTRL_REG4, 0x0C)
        # CTRL_REG5: BDU=1 so a reading's low and high bytes always belong together
        self._w(_CTRL_REG5, 0x40)
        # CTRL_REG3: MD=00 continuous conversion (leaves power-down, the reset default)
        self._w(_CTRL_REG3, 0x00)
        time.sleep_ms(110)  # first sample at 10 Hz

    def _r(self, reg, n):
        return self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, reg, n)

    def _w(self, reg, val):
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, reg, bytes([val]))

    def read_raw(self):
        """Raw signed counts (x, y, z)."""
        for _ in range(50):  # wait for ZYXDA, at most about 0.5 s
            if self._r(_STATUS_REG, 1)[0] & 0x08:
                break
            time.sleep_ms(10)
        d = self._r(_OUT_X_L | 0x80, 6)
        out = []
        for i in (0, 2, 4):
            v = d[i] | (d[i + 1] << 8)
            out.append(v - 65536 if v & 0x8000 else v)
        return tuple(out)

    def read(self):
        """Magnetic field (x, y, z) in gauss (1 gauss = 100 uT)."""
        x, y, z = self.read_raw()
        s = self._sens
        return x / s, y / s, z / s

    def read_ut(self):
        """Magnetic field (x, y, z) in microtesla."""
        return tuple(v * 100 for v in self.read())

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from lis3mdl import LIS3MDL

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
mag = LIS3MDL(i2c)
while True:
    x, y, z = mag.read()
    print('X=%.3f Y=%.3f Z=%.3f gauss' % (x, y, z))
    time.sleep(1)
